description: Minimal dashboard for zebby76/prometheus-s3-exporter 4.2.0, one row per exporter. Queries aggregate with max by (name) to drop scrape labels before the join. webtech_s3_exporter_up carries no labels of its own, so it is tied back to name through a join on webtech_s3_exporter_info. On OpenShift the exporter's namespace label collides with the scrape target's and is renamed exported_namespace, so this dashboard filters on name only.

panels.description: Current state of every bucket. Sorted by staleness, so the oldest figures rise to the top. CPU, Memory and Throttled come from cAdvisor and are tied to the bucket through exporter_info on (namespace, pod): they need a datasource that sees both container metrics and the exporter, i.e. Thanos Querier rather than the user-workload Prometheus alone. Connections/h, DNS, Errors/h and Main error come from the probe's diagnosis metrics: a reconnect every probe means the idle timeout in front of the storage is shorter than connectivity_interval; DNS in multiples of 5s means lost DNS queries.
panels.title: S3 buckets

panels.description: Probe latency against reconnects. A flat latency with reconnects steadily above zero means connectivity_interval is longer than the idle timeout in front of the storage system: every probe pays a fresh connection setup.
panels.title: Probe latency and reconnects
Probe errors by reason
panels.description: Failed probe attempts, retried ones included, by where they failed: dns, connect_timeout (no answer to the connection), connect (refused or reset), read_timeout, http_5xx, http_4xx. botocore prints the same message for a DNS failure and a refused connection; this tells them apart.

panels.title: Endpoint: DNS, TCP, TLS
panels.description: Each endpoint checked on its own every probe interval: its name resolved through the pod's resolver (search list and ndots included), a TCP connection, a TLS handshake for https. Steps at multiples of 5s in dns are lost DNS queries waiting out the resolver's timeout; bars are failed checks, by the phase that failed.

panels.title: Probe latency against new connections
panels.description: Only a new connection resolves the endpoint name and pays the TCP setup. A latency peak that coincides with a new-connection bar is DNS or connect time; a peak without one is the server or the network on an open connection.
Whether each probe reached the bucket.
panels.title: Reachability

panels.description: The probe's own account of each event: an outage with every attempt and its root cause, a recovery, an endpoint failing at dns, tcp or tls, a change of address, a certificate close to its end, a check that opened a connection or retried. Set the log selector variable to where the exporters' logs live.

targets.expr: ${log_selector} |~ "became unreachable|is reachable again|Endpoint .* failed at|resolves to|certificate of|new connection|failed in"

panels.title: Probe events

list.description: LogQL stream selector for the exporters' logs. The default matches the local stack; on OpenShift use e.g. {namespace="my-ns", container="s3-exporter"}.
list.label: Log selector
list.name: log_selector
